threads.body: [General] The module still advertises Camel support for `[2.19,3)` (`build.gradle.kts:9`), but Camel 2.19's `KafkaFetchRecords` has no `doRun()` method, so this matcher never applies there. Camel 2.19 batches therefore are not marked as Camel-owned and the Kafka client iterator advice still creates duplicate process spans. Match the 2.19 `run()` path as well, while guarding the null consumer seen on the newer outer `run()`.

replies.body:
Addressed in 3bd81da3ef8f0e4baf6fc33847b0dc8c4abd619c.

Analysis: Camel 2.19 initializes the consumer before entering run(), while Camel 2.20 and later initialize it inside run() and perform polling in doRun(). Matching both methods covers the supported range. The null guard makes the Camel 2.20+ wrapper invocation a no-op until doRun() starts with an initialized consumer.

Upsides: Camel 2.19 batches now use Camel delivery ownership, while newer Camel versions retain their existing ownership behavior without relying on suppressed null failures.

Downsides: Camel 2.20 and later execute one additional no-op advice call when the outer run() starts.

threads.body: With the `MessagingTelemetryState` propagation removed above, this process instrumenter now unconditionally records `messaging.client.consumed.messages` for every Camel delivery. When Kafka, JMS, or SQS client instrumentation already recorded the consumed-message signal, this emits a second count; consumed-message deduplication is explicitly separate from this ownership change and tracked in #20214. Preserve the existing signal-aware customization until that follow-up implements the replacement.

threads.body: [General] This handoff calls `SqsProcessTracing`, whose implementation recognizes deliveries with `messages instanceof TracingList`. With the agent's indy mode, Camel and AWS SDK instrumentations use separate module class loaders and therefore separate copies of `TracingList`; the Camel helper will see the AWS SDK's traced list as an ordinary `List`, so the SDK process span is not suppressed and Camel emits a duplicate process span. Put this handoff marker in shared/bootstrap state (or otherwise make it class-loader independent) and add an indy regression test.
